_about: Public-domain John Gregory Pike, General Baptist minister at Derby and secretary of the General Baptist Missionary Society, for the Word Hoard: Persuasives to Early Piety, A Guide for Young Disciples, The Consolations of Gospel Truth, Swedenborgianism Depicted, Religion and Eternal Life, The Divine Origin of Christianity, True Happiness, and his memoir of Charlotte Sutton. Texts are from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 132 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

pike-guide-young-disciples: A guide for young disciples of the Holy Saviour, in their way to immortality: forming a sequel to Persuasives to early piety (New York, American Tract Society, [182)
pike-consolations: Consolations of Gospel truth, exhibited in various interesting anecdotes respecting the dying hours of ... persons who gloried in the Cross of Christ (New York, Paul, 1823)
pike-swedenborgianism: Swedenborgianism Depicted in Its True Colors: Or, A Contrast Between the Holy Scriptures and the (Printed for the Publisher, 1834)
pike-religion-eternal-life: Religion and eternal life; or, Irreligion and perpetual ruin, the only alternative for mankind (New York, The American tract society, 1834)
pike-charlotte-sutton: Memoir of Mrs. Charlotte Sutton : a missionary to Orissa, East Indies (Boston / : Gould, Kendall & Lincoln, 1835)
pike-divine-origin: The divine origin of Christianity (Dover, Trustees of the Freewill Baptist Connection, 1836)
pike-true-happiness: True happiness : or, The excellence and power of early religion (New York : R. Carter, 1844)
